paper.title: F.784 Treasury Management Activity Report 2025/26
paper.note: Covering report is a 4-page brief. Substance lives in two companion papers already on disk and read in full: doc 39486 (Annex A, 14 pp, Annual Treasury Management Review) and doc 39487 (Annex B, 5 pp, Pooled Fund Investments). All figures below sourced from Annex A/B unless the covering report itself is cited. The same F.784 report is repeated at Audit Committee on 2 July 2026 (doc 39527/39528/39529) and at Full Council on 23 July 2026 (doc 39621/39622/39623 under a re-numbered F.791) — content identical, no re-read needed.

facts.value: £0 external borrowing at 31.3.26. No temporary loans, no PWLB, no market debt, no LOBOs, no other long-term liabilities. Position unchanged from 31.3.25; no borrowing taken out during 2025/26.
facts.note: Six independent presentations across Annex A all agree at zero (Table 1, Table 2, §5, Table 7, §9.7 debt row, §9.8). The PWLB price book returns no borrower matching 'Forest of Dean' — both sides tie at zero. This is not a live PWLB position; there is no loan book to reconcile.

facts.value: General Fund CFR £0 at 31.3.26 actual; forecast to rise to £4.220m (31.3.27), £6.090m (31.3.28) and £5.941m (31.3.29). Liability benchmark table forecasts external borrowing of £5.878m from 31.3.27, tapering to £5.508m by 31.3.29. Net loans requirement moves from £(14.191)m (net investor) at 31.3.26 to +£1.125m (net borrower) at 31.3.29.
facts.note: The Council is scheduled to become a first-time PWLB borrower over the strategy period. However Annex B §1.7 explicitly states the plan is to fund emerging capital pressure by selling pooled fund investments rather than borrowing: 'the potential sale of pooled fund investments will be evaluated in line with capital programme needs and timing considerations. To minimise financial impact, any divestment should ideally begin with the fund that presents the smallest capital loss, offers the lowest return, and is the most readily accessible.' Small figures either way.

facts.value: Total investments £14.349m at 31.3.26 (down from £16.064m at 31.3.25). Split: long-term £6.566m at 4.56%, short-term £2.139m at 4.14%, cash £5.644m at 4.14%. Whole-portfolio rate 4.57%. Detail: banks & building societies £0.306m at 3.51%; local authority £2.003m at 6.75%; money market funds £5.338m at 4.14%; CCLA Property £2.673m at 4.11%; CCLA Cautious Multi Asset £1.775m at 2.83%; Schroders Equity Income £0.944m at 6.25%; Fundamentum REIT £1.310m at 3.00%.
facts.note: Local Authority line at 6.75% is significantly higher than any other treasury asset in the book. Portfolio ranged between £12.865m and £27.480m during the year. Average investment portfolio £20.05m at outturn (Annex A §7).

facts.value: £6m original investment across three strategic pooled funds (CCLA Property £3m, CCLA Cautious Multi Asset £2m, Schroders Income Maximiser £1m) plus £2m in Fundamentum Social Housing REIT. Cumulative unrealised capital loss to date £1,434,283 (funds £714,283, REIT £720,000). Dividend income to date £2,285,293 across all four. 2025/26 dividend income £302,462 at 4.56% blended return on £8m original.
facts.note: IFRS 9 statutory override extended to 1 April 2029 for investments in place before 1 April 2024 (all four funds were entered between 2017 and 2019). Fundamentum REIT NAV drop 'mainly due to a reduction of around 20% in property valuations ... financial difficulties experienced by some housing associations in the specialist supported housing sector' — Annex B §1.8. CCLA Property fund has 6 months' notice; other two funds 2 business days'; REIT variable (direct, via Arlingclose network, or property sale).

facts.value: Investment income budget £849,000 (original), £789,000 (revised), actual £797,626 — surplus £8,626 vs revised, deficit £51,374 vs original. Overall return 4.57% (24/25 comparator 4.46%). Debt interest paid £2k on £25k budget.
facts.note: Covering §2.2 and Annex A §3.1 both foot to the £8,626 surplus. No borrowing was taken during the year so the £2k of debt interest paid appears to relate to a de minimis fee — the paper does not itemise it.

facts.value: Portfolio average credit A+ at 31.3.26 (target A-). Liquidity £11.860m within 3 months (target £5m). Long-term principal invested £8m (limit £10m). Interest rate exposure ±£138,078 on 1% shift (limit ±£220,000). All 10 investment sub-limits complied. Debt: authorised limit £10m (per §9.8) or £20m (per §8 Table 7), operational boundary £5m or £10m — the two tables disagree; actual £0 all year, so no compliance question.

Adviser: Arlingclose Ltd. Bank Rate fell 0.75% from 4.50% (1 April 2025) to 3.75% (31 March 2026). Arlingclose's post-March MPC forecast at Annex A §2.7: 'Bank Rate will be held at 3.75%' with near-term upside risks from the US/Israel-Iran conflict outlook.
facts.note: DMADF deposits ranged 4.13-4.56% during 25/26; money market rates 3.81-4.50%. Bank Rate today (2026-08-15) is 3.75% — the hold has continued to date.

status.note: Read in full: covering report (doc 39485, 4pp), Annex A Annual Treasury Management Review (doc 39486, 14pp), Annex B Pooled Fund Investments (doc 39487, 5pp). All three PDFs held locally; no fetching from the council site. The paper is thin from a PWLB perspective because the Council is debt-free: no external borrowing at any point in 2025/26, no PWLB loans on our price book (both sides tie at zero — nothing to reconcile). Forward CFR ramp of £4-6m from 27/28 is small and Annex B §1.7 explicitly states the Council's plan is to divest pooled funds rather than borrow to meet emerging capital pressure. Balance-sheet identity trivially holds: CFR £0 − external £0 − OLTL £0 = £0 internal borrowing, against £14.349m of net investments. Per PIPELINE.md 'a thin note is far better than a padded one' — draft NO email, this is a correct outcome. Officer address IS published (Andrew Knott, andrew.knott@publicagroup.uk) so this council is not blocked on address; it is blocked on hook. Should the Council actually enter the PWLB market when forecast, or should a mid-year report show discretionary divestment triggered, revisit.
